stories.title: Simple ‘Soil Steaming’ Found as Effective Replacement for Chemicals in Organic Strawberry Farming
stories.label: agriculture
stories.summary: Researchers in California have found a surprisingly simple way to grow bigger, healthier organic strawberries without harsh chemical fumigants. By blasting the soil with hot steam before planting, they can kill off pests and disease the same way old-fashioned fumigants do, but without the toxic residue. Field trials showed this steam treatment gave strawberry farmers yields they could count on, a huge win for organic growers who've struggled with unreliable harvests. It's a low-tech fix that could make organic strawberries both more available and more affordable. Great news for anyone who loves fruit grown without chemicals.
stories.why_good: A real, tested farming method that already worked in trials, cutting chemical use while helping organic growers get reliable harvests.

stories.title: Brazil Ends Long Tradition of 6-Day Workweek via Constitutional Amendment
stories.label: government
stories.summary: Brazil's senate just voted overwhelmingly, 75 to 1, to pass a constitutional amendment ending the country's long-standing 6-day workweek. Millions of full-time workers there had been putting in 44 hours a week, more than many other nations require. Now the standard moves closer to the kind of 40-hour week common elsewhere, giving workers an extra day to rest, see family, or just breathe. It's a rare case of a government actually following through to improve everyday life for its citizens.
stories.why_good: A concrete law has passed that directly improves quality of life for millions of workers, decided through ordinary legislative process rather than conflict.

stories.title: Mozambique Protects the 'Butterfly Forest' of Mount Mabu, Home to 200 Species
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: Mozambique's government has officially protected 23,000 acres of lush rainforest on Mount Mabu, known as the 'butterfly forest' for its stunning diversity of winged creatures. The decree, signed in August, creates the Mount Mabu Community Conservation Area, safeguarding more than 200 butterfly species along with countless other plants and animals found in this remote, misty mountain range. It's one of the wettest and most biologically rich places in southern Africa, and now it has the legal protection it needs to stay that way. Local communities will be involved in managing the land, so people and nature both benefit.
stories.why_good: A real government decree permanently protects a biodiversity hotspot and the communities who live there.
